title: IL HB1806: THERAPY RESOURCES OVERSIGHT

obligations: A licensed professional using artificial intelligence must maintain full responsibility for all interactions, outputs, and data use associated with the system and satisfy the requirements of subsection (b) (Section 15(a))

A licensed professional using artificial intelligence to assist in providing supplementary support where the client's therapeutic session is recorded or transcribed must inform the patient or the patient's legally authorized representative in writing that artificial intelligence will be used and the specific purpose of the artificial intelligence tool or system, and must obtain consent to the use of artificial intelligence (Section 15(b))
A licensed professional may use artificial intelligence only to the extent the use meets the requirements of Section 15 (Section 20(b))

All records kept by a licensed professional and all communications between an individual seeking therapy or psychotherapy services and a licensed professional shall be confidential and shall not be disclosed except as required under the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act (Section 25)
prohibitions: An individual, corporation, or entity may not provide, advertise, or otherwise offer therapy or psychotherapy services, including through the use of Internet based artificial intelligence, to the public in this State unless the therapy or psychotherapy services are conducted by an individual who is a licensed professional (Section 20(a))

No licensed professional shall be permitted to use artificial intelligence to assist in providing supplementary support in therapy or psychotherapy where the client's therapeutic session is recorded or transcribed unless the patient or the patient's legally authorized representative is informed in writing and provides consent (Section 15(b))
A licensed professional may not allow artificial intelligence to make independent therapeutic decisions (Section 20(b)(1))
A licensed professional may not allow artificial intelligence to directly interact with clients in any form of therapeutic communication (Section 20(b)(2))
A licensed professional may not allow artificial intelligence to generate therapeutic recommendations or treatment plans without review and approval by the licensed professional (Section 20(b)(3))
A licensed professional may not allow artificial intelligence to detect emotions or mental states (Section 20(b)(4))
Records and communications shall not be disclosed except as required under the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act (Section 25)

Department: the Department of Financial and Professional Regulation (Section 10)

Licensed professional: an individual who holds a valid license issued by this State to provide therapy or psychotherapy services, including a licensed clinical psychologist, licensed clinical social worker, licensed social worker, licensed professional counselor, licensed clinical professional counselor, licensed marriage and family therapist, certified alcohol and other drug counselor authorized to provide therapy or psychotherapy services, licensed professional music therapist, licensed advanced practice psychiatric nurse as defined in Section 1-101.3 of the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Code, and any other professional authorized by this State to provide therapy or psychotherapy services, except for a physician (Section 10)

Peer support: services provided by individuals with lived experience of mental health conditions or recovery from substance use that are intended to offer encouragement, understanding, and guidance without clinical intervention (Section 10)

Religious counseling: counseling provided by clergy members, pastoral counselors, or other religious leaders acting within the scope of their religious duties if the services are explicitly faith based and are not represented as clinical mental health services or therapy or psychotherapy services (Section 10)

Therapy or psychotherapy services: services provided to diagnose, treat, or improve an individual's mental health or behavioral health; does not include religious counseling or peer support (Section 10)

If using AI, restrict its use to administrative support or supplementary support and ensure a licensed professional maintains full responsibility for all interactions, outputs, and data use (Section 15(a))

If AI is used for supplementary support where client sessions are recorded or transcribed, provide written notice to the patient or legally authorized representative that AI will be used and the specific purpose, and obtain consent before use (Section 15(b))

Passed 2025-08-01. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

This Act restricts who may provide therapy or psychotherapy services in Illinois to licensed professionals and limits how artificial intelligence may be used in those services. It permits licensed professionals to use AI only for administrative or supplementary support, subject to notice and consent requirements when sessions are recorded or transcribed, and prohibits AI from engaging in therapeutic communication or making independent clinical decisions. It also establishes confidentiality requirements and civil penalties for violations.

Who it applies to

  • Licensed professionals as defined in Section 10
  • Individuals, corporations, or entities that provide, advertise, or offer therapy or psychotherapy services to the public in Illinois (Section 20(a))
  • The Department of Financial and Professional Regulation (Section 30)

Effective date

upon becoming law

Key definitions

  • Administrative support: tasks performed to assist a licensed professional in the delivery of therapy or psychotherapy services that do not involve communication, including managing appointment scheduling and reminders, processing billing and insurance claims, and drafting general communications related to therapy logistics that do not include therapeutic advice (Section 10)
  • Artificial intelligence: has the meaning given to that term in Section 2-101 of the Illinois Human Rights Act (Section 10)
  • Consent: a clear, explicit affirmative act by an individual that unambiguously communicates the individual's express, freely given, informed, voluntary, specific, and unambiguous written agreement, including a written agreement provided by electronic means, and is revocable by the individual; does not include acceptance of a general or broad terms of use agreement, hovering over, muting, pausing, or closing digital content, or agreement obtained through deceptive actions (Section 10)
  • Department: the Department of Financial and Professional Regulation (Section 10)
  • Licensed professional: an individual who holds a valid license issued by this State to provide therapy or psychotherapy services, including a licensed clinical psychologist, licensed clinical social worker, licensed social worker, licensed professional counselor, licensed clinical professional counselor, licensed marriage and family therapist, certified alcohol and other drug counselor authorized to provide therapy or psychotherapy services, licensed professional music therapist, licensed advanced practice psychiatric nurse as defined in Section 1-101.3 of the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Code, and any other professional authorized by this State to provide therapy or psychotherapy services, except for a physician (Section 10)
  • Peer support: services provided by individuals with lived experience of mental health conditions or recovery from substance use that are intended to offer encouragement, understanding, and guidance without clinical intervention (Section 10)
  • Religious counseling: counseling provided by clergy members, pastoral counselors, or other religious leaders acting within the scope of their religious duties if the services are explicitly faith based and are not represented as clinical mental health services or therapy or psychotherapy services (Section 10)
  • Supplementary support: tasks performed to assist a licensed professional in the delivery of therapy or psychotherapy services that do not involve therapeutic communication and that are not administrative support, including preparing and maintaining client records, analyzing anonymized data to track client progress or identify trends subject to review by a licensed professional, and identifying and organizing external resources or referrals for client use (Section 10)
  • Therapeutic communication: any verbal, nonverbal, or written interaction conducted in a clinical or professional setting that is intended to diagnose, treat, or address an individual's mental, emotional, or behavioral health concerns, including direct interactions with clients to understand or reflect their thoughts, emotions, or experiences, providing guidance, therapeutic strategies, or interventions, offering emotional support, reassurance, or empathy, collaborating with clients to develop or modify therapeutic goals or treatment plans, and offering behavioral feedback intended to promote psychological growth or address mental health conditions (Section 10)
  • Therapy or psychotherapy services: services provided to diagnose, treat, or improve an individual's mental health or behavioral health; does not include religious counseling or peer support (Section 10)
  • Permitted use of artificial intelligence: the use of artificial intelligence tools or systems by a licensed professional to assist in providing administrative support or supplementary support in therapy or psychotherapy services where the licensed professional maintains full responsibility for all interactions, outputs, and data use associated with the system and satisfies the requirements of subsection (b) (Section 15)

Obligations

  • A licensed professional using artificial intelligence must maintain full responsibility for all interactions, outputs, and data use associated with the system and satisfy the requirements of subsection (b) (Section 15(a))
  • A licensed professional using artificial intelligence to assist in providing supplementary support where the client's therapeutic session is recorded or transcribed must inform the patient or the patient's legally authorized representative in writing that artificial intelligence will be used and the specific purpose of the artificial intelligence tool or system, and must obtain consent to the use of artificial intelligence (Section 15(b))
  • A licensed professional may use artificial intelligence only to the extent the use meets the requirements of Section 15 (Section 20(b))
  • All records kept by a licensed professional and all communications between an individual seeking therapy or psychotherapy services and a licensed professional shall be confidential and shall not be disclosed except as required under the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act (Section 25)

Prohibitions

  • An individual, corporation, or entity may not provide, advertise, or otherwise offer therapy or psychotherapy services, including through the use of Internet based artificial intelligence, to the public in this State unless the therapy or psychotherapy services are conducted by an individual who is a licensed professional (Section 20(a))
  • No licensed professional shall be permitted to use artificial intelligence to assist in providing supplementary support in therapy or psychotherapy where the client's therapeutic session is recorded or transcribed unless the patient or the patient's legally authorized representative is informed in writing and provides consent (Section 15(b))
  • A licensed professional may not allow artificial intelligence to make independent therapeutic decisions (Section 20(b)(1))
  • A licensed professional may not allow artificial intelligence to directly interact with clients in any form of therapeutic communication (Section 20(b)(2))
  • A licensed professional may not allow artificial intelligence to generate therapeutic recommendations or treatment plans without review and approval by the licensed professional (Section 20(b)(3))
  • A licensed professional may not allow artificial intelligence to detect emotions or mental states (Section 20(b)(4))
  • Records and communications shall not be disclosed except as required under the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act (Section 25)

Penalties and enforcement

The Department of Financial and Professional Regulation has authority to investigate any actual, alleged, or suspected violation of this Act (Section 30(b)). Any individual, corporation, or entity found in violation shall pay a civil penalty to the Department in an amount not to exceed $10,000 per violation, as determined by the Department, with penalties assessed based on the degree of harm and the circumstances of the violation; the civil penalty shall be assessed by the Department after a hearing in accordance with Section 2105-100 of the Department of Professional Regulation Law of the Civil Administrative Code of Illinois; the violator shall pay the civil penalty within 60 days after the date of an order by the Department imposing the civil penalty; the order constitutes a judgment and may be filed and executed in the same manner as any judgment from a court of record (Section 30(a)). The text does not state a private right of action.

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organization deploying AI to provide therapy or psychotherapy services to the public in Illinois must ensure those services are conducted by a licensed professional; AI alone cannot provide, advertise, or offer such services, including through Internet based AI (Section 20(a))
  • AI may be used by a licensed professional only for administrative support or supplementary support, and the licensed professional must maintain full responsibility for all interactions, outputs, and data use associated with the system (Section 15(a))
  • AI cannot directly interact with clients in any form of therapeutic communication, make independent therapeutic decisions, generate therapeutic recommendations or treatment plans without review and approval by the licensed professional, or detect emotions or mental states (Section 20(b))
  • If AI is used to assist in supplementary support where a client's therapeutic session is recorded or transcribed, the organization must ensure the patient or legally authorized representative is informed in writing that AI will be used and the specific purpose, and obtains consent (Section 15(b))
  • Records and communications related to therapy must remain confidential and may be disclosed only as required under the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act (Section 25)
  • Violations can result in civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation assessed by the Department after a hearing (Section 30(a))

Notable exemptions

  • Religious counseling (Section 35(1))
  • Peer support (Section 35(2))
  • Self help materials and educational resources that are available to the public and do not purport to offer therapy or psychotherapy services (Section 35(3))

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether the organization offers therapy or psychotherapy services to the public in Illinois; if so, ensure those services are conducted by a licensed professional as defined in Section 10 (Section 20(a))
  • If using AI, restrict its use to administrative support or supplementary support and ensure a licensed professional maintains full responsibility for all interactions, outputs, and data use (Section 15(a))
  • If AI is used for supplementary support where client sessions are recorded or transcribed, provide written notice to the patient or legally authorized representative that AI will be used and the specific purpose, and obtain consent before use (Section 15(b))
  • Configure and monitor AI systems to prevent independent therapeutic decisions, direct therapeutic communication with clients, generation of therapeutic recommendations or treatment plans without licensed professional review and approval, and detection of emotions or mental states (Section 20(b))
  • Maintain confidentiality of all records and communications in accordance with the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act (Section 25)
  • Prepare for potential Department investigation and civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation; ensure procedures for responding to Department inquiries and hearings (Section 30)
